title: embed-rerank-dim-investigation-notebook-omar
body:
SUMMARY
Quick lab notebook capturing commands, observations, and hypotheses for the rerank/embeddings anomaly observed on 2026-05-27 (dim mismatch + intermittent latency spikes). Personal notes — messy, iterative. Goal: record minimal repro attempts and next actions for handoff.

BACKGROUND
- Customer-facing rerank endpoint started returning 400s from downstream scoring service at ~2026-05-27T14:18Z while a subset of embeddings had shape/length disagreements.
- Concurrent: production embedding provider reported a small deploy (python-sdk v1.8.3 -> v1.9.0) and we saw elevated p99 latency on dedupe/merge pipeline.
- Incident ticket: RED-4532 (linked).

OBSERVED SYMPTOMS (raw)
- API error snippet from rerank service: "ValueError: embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024"
- Client stack: nodejs backend (embed+rerank flow) -> Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint -> local reranker that expects fixed dim 1536.
- Sporadic latencies: p50 normal (~30ms), p99 spiked to 2.1s for rerank step, correlated with batches > 8 or when batching client used new SDK.
- Memory spikes on worker-host-12 (serving-runtime pool) + OOM-swap events recorded on 2026-05-27T14:20-14:27

TIMELINE (what I ran locally; timestamps UTC)
- 2026-05-27T15:05: Started a local repro harness (python) to call hosted embeddings in small batches.
- 2026-05-27T15:07: First mismatch seen when I concurrently ran two different clients (py v1.9.0 + js v2.3.1).
- 2026-05-27T15:10: Reproduced dimension mismatch with python client only when using batch_size=16 + streaming set to True.
- 2026-05-27T15:25: Disabled streaming, ran batch_size sweep, mismatch only when batch_size >= 12.

REPRO STEPS (minimal)
- env: python 3.10, py-sdk v1.9.0 (pip install redwood-sdk==1.9.0), node v18 for comparison.
- simple script (local):
  1) pipenv shell
  2) cat save_repro.py:
     from redwood import Embeddings
     e = Embeddings(api_key=\"REDACTED\")
     data = [\"short doc\"] * 16
     resp = e.create(model=\"open-embed-1536\", input=data, batch_size=16, streaming=True)
     print([len(v) for v in resp.data])
  3) expected: all 1536. observed: mix of 1536 and 1024 entries.

COMMANDS TRIED (local & remote)
- curl (prod): curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["a","b","c"]}' | jq 
  -> always returned 1536 for single inputs.
- py repro (above) -> shows mismatch on batch_size >= 12 + streaming True.
- swap client version: pip install redwood-sdk==1.8.3 -> mismatch disappeared for batch_size 16.
- node client repro (node-sdk v2.3.1) with batch 16 + stream true -> intermittent mismatch (less frequent than python).
- env var test: REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS unset vs set=65536 no change.

NOTES FROM LOGS (excerpts)
- serving-runtime logs (worker-host-12):
  [2026-05-27T14:20:12Z] INFO batcher: starting batch id=bf3 size=16 model=open-embed-1536 stream=true
  [2026-05-27T14:20:12Z] WARN kernel-selector: quantized-kernel mismatch detected; fallback to smaller-kernel
  [2026-05-27T14:20:12Z] ERROR serializer: expected 1536 floats but wrote 1024 for entry idx=7

HYPOTHESES
1) Partial serializer edge case when streaming=true and batch boundary changes during chunked assembly -> legacy path pads/truncates to different output dim (e.g., uses model variant open-embed-1024 under fallback).
2) Kernel/quantization fallback path returns embeddings for a smaller model variant (1024) but downstream code assumes consistent dim; fallback not signaled to client.
3) In-proc batching race when two different models or configs hit the same GPU and batcher reuses buffer sizes incorrectly (buffer reuse bug).
4) SDK change in v1.9.0 altered streaming framing and introduced a header misread that causes the server to interpret request as model=open-embed-1024 for some messages.
5) Latency spikes tied to fallback kernel selection causing additional CPU-based post-processing on host leading to p99 blow-ups.

EXPERIMENTS RUN (results)
- A: Reproduced on local against prod endpoint with same api key using py-sdk v1.9.0, streamed batch 16 -> mismatch occurs ~70% of runs.
- B: Re-ran with streaming=False, batch_size=16 -> mismatch gone. Suggests streaming path implicated.
- C: Downgraded to py-sdk v1.8.3 -> mismatch gone even with streaming True. Suggests SDK change important.
- D: Force model param to explicit string \"open-embed-1536-fp16\" (explicit variant) -> mismatch reduced but still occasional.
- E: Queried serving-runtime metrics during repro: kernel_fallback_count increased by 23x for those batches that produced 1024 dims.

TEMP FIX / MITIGATION (short-term)
- Revert python-sdk to 1.8.3 on client side where possible (customer rollout patch).
- On server, add defensive validation: if embedding length != expected -> respond 500 + diagnostics header (X-Embed-Dim-Observed:1024).
- For rerank service: make reranker tolerant to variable dims by rejecting or re-embedding; short-term inject guard that logs and increments an error counter rather than crashing.

NEXT ACTIONS (priority order)
1) Split investigation: infra/serving team to look at kernel-selector and serializer code paths for streaming + batch boundary reuse (assign to @Maya).
2) SDK team: diff between 1.8.3 and 1.9.0 streaming framing and confirm whether new framing breaks backward compatibility (assign to @Aisha).
3) Add server-side quick guard (PR) that validates dim and returns clear error instead of producing mismatched vectors. Small PR: serving-runtime/validate-embed-dim (blocking but low-risk).
4) Add telemetry: emit X-Embed-Variant and kernel_fallback boolean into request logs for rapid triage.
5) Customer comms: recommend pinning to py-sdk v1.8.3 and toggling streaming=False until fix rolled. Coordinate with CS.

NOTES TO SELF / TODOs
- Re-run node repro with network sniffing to ensure client frames are identical to python (wireshark + tcpdump example saved to /tmp/sniff.pcap).
- Prepare minimal failing test case for serving-runtime repo (go/py test depending on serializer). Aim to have unit test reproducing buffer reuse.
- Check GPU driver upgrade logs around 2026-05-27 to be sure no kernel-level change.
- Keep an eye on p99 telemetry post-mitigation.

RANDOM OBSERVATIONS (misc)
- I saw one log line where two different model names were present in same batch start message (likely aggregator bug).
- The mismatch index often occurred at entry idx ~7-9 when batch size 16; maybe half-batch boundary issue.

ATTACHMENTS / FILES I CREATED
- save_repro.py (local) — path: ~/work/repro/embed_dim/save_repro.py
- tcpdump capture: ~/work/repro/embed_dim/sniff_20260527.pcap
- quick server patch PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/924 (draft)

FINAL NOTE
This is a working notebook. The strong lead right now is interaction between the new SDK streaming framing + server path that handles streaming/batching; focus triage there first. I will sync with Maya & Aisha in the 11:30 stand to hand off the reproduction and debug traces.

-- Omar
